common_name: Silurian Dichotomous Sporophyte Stem (Oldest Vascular Tracheids)

phenomenon_scale.label: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Cooksonia pertoni (1.3 µm, detail scale)
phenomenon_scale.note: Assigned detail scale. Not a length measured by Edwards, Davies & Axe 1992.

predecessor.name: pre-vascular cooksonioid axis
predecessor.change: Equal diffusion, sigma_max < 0, no selected 1.3 µm band.

successor.name: Rhynia gwynne-vaughanii
successor.change: Longer activator diffusion length raises lambda_c from 1.339 µm to about 1.695 µm.

boundary_conditions: Periodic on the unrolled tracheid circumference; Neumann along the axis.

equations.pde: du/dt = D_u Laplacian(u) + a - u + u^2 v; dv/dt = D_v Laplacian(v) + b - u^2 v
equations.dispersion: sigma_+(k) = largest real-part eigenvalue of J - k^2 diag(D_u, D_v)
equations.wavelength: lambda_c = 2 pi / k_c, scaled so lambda_c = 1.339e-6 m

empirical_claims: Edwards, Davies & Axe 1992 demonstrated a vascular conducting strand in Cooksonia pertoni, with tracheids that bear annular to spiral thickenings.
Edwards 2003 reviews annular, spiral and scalariform-like walls in early tracheophytes and states that few fossils are identical to extant xylem.
Turing 1952: a homogeneous steady state stable without diffusion can be unstable with diffusion, selecting a finite wavenumber.
This script's 1.339 µm wavelength is the assigned detail scale, not a measurement copied from those papers.

pass2_results.note: Quadratic peak on a 0.5 degree template grid. Wall bands imprinted after the shell-power match.

specimen.credit: Amgueddfa Cymru – National Museum Wales, via Wikimedia Commons
specimen.description: Silurian early land plant fossil (Cooksonia pertoni)

second_specimen.role: template-angle sensitivity check, not the fitness target

reported_in_source: Vascular strand and annular/spiral tracheids in C. pertoni (Edwards, Davies & Axe 1992).
Turing dispersion relation and Schnakenberg kinetics.
reconstructed_in_script: Parameters chosen so the fastest mode is 1.339 µm.
Isotomous axis on a spectrum-matched matrix for comparison with the museum photograph.
does_not_claim: That 1.3 µm was measured on the fossil.
That the photograph resolves wall bands.
That the 73 µm sibling parameters apply here.
